items.headline: Logan: Fed needs 'at least two more' hikes — voter puts a number on the tightening path

items.headline: Warsh presser knocks dollar off its two-week high — DXY slides to 102.05
bullets: Warsh's presser unwound the dollar's climb into the decision: the DXY fell from just above 102.40 to near 102.05, its low of the day, and was trading near 102.10 at the last update — a ~0.3%+ intraday leg, taking it under Wednesday's starting level near 102.35.

The dovish tilt: Warsh said price stability 'doesn't hinge on any one calendar date or an isolated data point,' that credit conditions have tightened, and that swap inflation compensation is 'going the right way'; his prepared line was that more information will help determine the appropriate stance — yet December hike pricing stayed near 86–90%, so this reads as a softer tone, not a December walk-back.

Also announced: from 2027 one FOMC meeting a year will be a strategy session with no rate vote (six policy-setting meetings in 2028) — fewer dates on which the Fed can move. Warsh framed September's hike as removing 'a dose of accommodation,' leaving the stance still accommodative.

items.headline: NYT: US/Israel drew up post-midterm Iran strike plans; Houthi strikes kill at Dammam airport and Shaybah oilfield
bullets: The New York Times (reported Wednesday, via multiple relays): US and Israeli militaries have drawn up specific plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms -- targets include nuclear sites, missile/drone arsenal and energy infrastructure; Hegseth met Netanyahu in Israel this week; the buildup including three carriers is expected to be in place by early November. Trump has not approved and has vetoed similar plans repeatedly this year.

After the ordered departure: Saudi energy ministry said debris from the interception of a drone targeting Aramco's Shaybah oilfield killed 2 (a Filipino and a Nepali) and injured 2; Reuters also reports a Houthi attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport killed 1 and injured 8.

FX still quiet: USD/JPY ~158.1, DXY ~101.7, Brent $109.92 -- no repricing, so Flash only, no chat ping.

items.headline: US Treasury sanctions Karnakis & Karnakis law firm + Iran shadow-fleet network (Operation Economic Outcast)
bullets: OFAC designated Greece/Panama law firm Karnakis & Karnakis, 5 individuals, Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents, and blocked 9 vessels under EO 13902 — accused of concealing Iranian oil, petrochemical and steel shipments (Treasury, Oct 21).
FinCEN issued its first-ever admin subpoena under 31 USC 5318(k) probing a Greek bank's Iran ties, plus info requests to six other European banks over Iran-linked relationships.
Still the enforcement lane, not the strike lane: Reuters notes Washington has 'held off striking Iran this month' and is running the blockade + sanction waves instead — oil price reaction nil so far.
